payload.analysis: Documented 4.5-second ventricular pause is the leading cause of dizziness/near-syncope via cerebral hypoperfusion. Medication-induced hypotension is secondary given low BP on amlodipine and improvement after withdrawal. payload.report: The patient's new-onset dizziness and near-syncope are best explained by the Zio-documented 4.5-second ventricular pause with junctional escape, which likely caused cerebral hypoperfusion (node-8 supports node-9). This arrhythmia is the leading hypothesis (confidence 0.70) and refutes medication-induced hypotension as the sole cause, despite prior low blood pressure on amlodipine and improvement after withdrawal. Graft dysfunction and autonomic dysregulation are unlikely because cardiac exam was unremarkable, symptoms improved after amlodipine cessation, and no orthostatic measurements support them. Therefore, ventricular pause/junctional escape arrhythmia is the most probable independent cause.
